TraceRouter++: Causal Semantic Routing Realignment via Optimal Transport

Trace safety-relevant causal routes and softly realign selected activation distributions toward safe references using a coordinate-wise optimal transport approximation.

Shi Chuancheng

November 3, 2026 ·TPAMI 2026CCF-A ·4-minute read ·Read the paper ·PDF
1Why this matters 2How it works 3What the study finds 4What this means

The short version

An unsafe behavior can travel through a network rather than reside in one isolated neuron. TraceRouter++ identifies safety-relevant routes and changes how their activations are distributed. The aim is to steer those routes toward safe-reference behavior while limiting the disturbance introduced at the intervention point.

The journal extension adds optimal-transport-based soft realignment to the Discover–Trace–Realign pipeline. It uses tractable coordinate-wise quantile mappings: this aligns selected marginals, rather than solving a general joint transport problem.

99.5%Mean LLaMA3 defense success rate
3 model familiesLLMs, MLLMs, and diffusion models
Optimal transportSoft activation realignment

Identifying a harmful route and deciding how to change its activation are complementary parts of safety intervention.

Why this matters

Suppressing an isolated feature can leave alternative propagation routes available and can also disturb useful computation. A route-level intervention makes both the location and the form of the modification explicit: where safety-relevant information travels, and how the selected activations should change.

How it works

  1. Discover a sensitive onset layer from attention divergence, then use a sparse autoencoder to isolate interpretable routing features.
  2. Trace downstream causal influence with feature influence scores, selecting routes supported by intervention evidence.
  3. Realign the selected activation marginals toward safe-reference marginals with an optimal transport approximation, leaving unselected coordinates unchanged at that intervention point.

What the study finds

On the reported LLM attack suite, average defense success rates reach 99.5 ± 0.3% for LLaMA3-8B-Instruct and 98.8 ± 0.3% for Mistral-7B-Instruct. The paper also evaluates multimodal language models and diffusion models.

Utility measurements accompany the safety results: Global-MMLU-Lite changes by −0.4 and −0.6 percentage points on the two language models. These empirical trade-offs are distinct from the local guarantee that unselected activation coordinates are preserved.

What this means

The insight is to treat safety control as a problem of shaping information flow. Causal tracing identifies a target for intervention, while distributional realignment provides an alternative to simply deleting the target signal. This connects mechanistic analysis with a more selective control objective.

The boundary is equally informative. Coordinate-wise transport does not generally preserve joint dependencies, and later layers can mix selected and unselected coordinates. Safety and utility therefore remain outcomes to measure, rather than consequences guaranteed by local sparsity alone.
